newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone off on mobile phone levy fears.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone off on mobile phone levy fears.

text.p: Shares in Vodafone Plc and Orange Plc stumbled at the open on Wednesday on press reports that the government would introduce a levy on mobile phones, dealers said.

But the shares climbed off their worst levels set at the open after UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said plans to reform the way it charges for use of the radio spectrum did not amount to a tax on mobile phone users or taxi cabs.
At 0808 GMT, Vodafone shares were down 5-1/2p to 276, while Orange shares eased 3-1/2p to 220. Shares of Telewest Communications also fell to 77-1/2.
The Financial Times said one of 26 bills to be announced in the Queen's Speech today would impose a levy that would increase the cost of operators' overheads by 10p per phone per week.
